retrieval.statement: Compared with the two reference fine-tunes, this model shows a consistent degradation on instruction-constrained prompts: it more often violates exact lexical/format requirements, adds unrequested headings/structure, mishandles continuations, and sometimes rejects or comments on requested constraints. It also more often invents concrete unsupported factual details about real-world entities and institutions, while occasionally being oddly cautious/minimal or choosing different interpretations for ambiguous/non-English prompts. On coding tasks it is more prone to requirement/interface drift and serious algorithmic mistakes, including wrong pointer movement, sorting by absolute value when not requested, retaining recursion despite stack-overflow constraints, changing function signatures or data fields, and producing incomplete/incorrect implementations. These differences appear concentrated in the detector-selected prompts and go beyond ordinary seed-level variation.
